BLOCKER: AC/owner mismatch: AC requires `owner core/execution_trail.py` and `python -m core.execution_trail show`, but the design ships `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py`; `python -m core.execution_trail` cannot resolve. AC 1 and 2 are not met as written.

Silent best-effort hook: a failed trail write drops required evidence (e.g. `delivery`/`completion`) with no failure signal, yet the completion gate then fails the item — gate outcome becomes dependent on an unlogged side channel rather than a checked contract.
MAJOR: Dependency inversion: `core/backlog.py` (shipped core) invoking a `scripts/dev` hook makes core depend on dev tooling; failure coupling and reload/ordering semantics are undefined.
No stated invariant for `seq` uniqueness/monotonicity across concurrent writers; a per-item lock alone does not prove ordering, and no concurrency/append test is listed.

Completion gate enforces only a subset (`gate0/design_review/gate1/diff_review/gate2/tests`); `planning`, `pr`, `merge`, `delivery`, `completion`, `implementation`, `code_review`, `precheck` are in the AC stage list but unenforced — out-of-order or absent late stages pass the gate.
No observability plan for trail writes (metric/log/counter on append failure, hook miss, lock contention); without it, "best-effort" is undiagnosable in production runs.

Test scope covers only `test_execution_trail.py` happy path; recurring review findings call out missing coverage for render/disposition helpers and check failure paths (`DEFERRED` without follow-up, out-of-order detection).
`architect_review.render_gate_view` reuse appears to reach into private helpers (`_render_review`, `_item_dispositions`) — cross-module reuse of private API is a maintainability and contract risk.
MINOR: No redaction/retention policy for `refs`/`summary`/token usage persisted in the durable trail store (checklist items 9, 4).
Append-only JSON has no size bound, rotation, or compaction; long-lived items grow unbounded.
Usage "not captured" vs. zero semantics not defined for partially captured sessions (mixed sources in one trail).
"next backlog item" and "total time" in the final table have no defined behavior for partial/legacy/incomplete trails.
Rollback leaves `config/store-registry.json` and `config/ci-cd-gates.json` referencing a removed tool — restore path for config not stated.
NIT: Checklist guardrail questions (backup/restore before any destructive step, SPOF/alert lead-time, needs_api) are not explicitly answered in the design text even though the design guardrails require it.
Naming: item in_scope says `scripts/dev/*` while AC says `core/*`; pick one and align all three of AC, in_scope, and affected_files.
SUMMARY: Solid direction: append-only registered store, tool-written evidence, and a fail-able completion check are the right shape, and reuse of `architect_review` render + store registry is good.

Top risks: (1) AC module path/owner is contradicted by the design, (2) best-effort writes silently corrupt gate evidence with no observability, (3) the completion gate enforces only ~6 of 14 mandated stages, so ordering integrity is not actually guaranteed.
Must resolve the owner mismatch and define the write-failure contract (log/metric + gate behavior) before Gate 1.5.
